summary: CKGSB's global marketing push is now squarely focused on China-based programs—Asia Star and the new Intelligent China—with search visibility and the knowledge website redesign as the twin engines, while this week's urgent fixes are clearing Outlook lockouts and finalizing the Knowledge site before launch.
summaryDetail: The top priority is the China-first program strategy: Asia Star and Intelligent China are the lead horses for search visibility (targeting top-5 rankings for China business school queries), with US partnerships on hold and Berkeley a possible third priority. Joseph is drafting the target prompts and analyzing Asia Star participant profiles/CRM hot leads to sharpen this, while the team must obtain the Google Ads conversion tracking brief and prioritize both programs in the upcoming audit. The knowledge website redesign is in final fixes—Joseph needs to share the HTML inspiration file, the team holds a 30-minute feedback session to mark comments, and Joker makes design changes; remaining launch blockers include publication news, She Innovates design consistency, and frame lines. This week's urgent operational issue is the Outlook account lockout: the team must delete/re-add accounts, update saved passwords on all devices, re-login on mobile, and contact JSB to confirm backend unlock. Upcoming: finalize the English obituary for Professor Jon Liao, update women's figures across programs with Deng Gang's latest data, and review the YouTube channel enhancement document—all while keeping the two-menu Knowledge/School structure and dispersing videos by topic.

decisions.text: Re-login and update passwords on all devices to prevent repeated account lockouts.
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic instead.
Keep the two-menu structure (Knowledge and School) with School menu top-right in gray.
Bring BCI and BSI indices into the knowledge section, similar to the school homepage banner.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Asia Star and Intelligent China are the top two program priorities; US programs (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) are secondary, with Berkeley as a possible third priority.
US partnership programs to be put on hold initially, focusing on China programs first.
No need to involve legal in the PRME data security incident at this point, as no real damage has occurred.
